newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fluor affiliate said in Argentine contract.
newsitem.headline: Fluor affiliate said in Argentine contract.

text.p: The U.S.-Argentine joint venture Fluor Daniel SADE has been awarded the engineering, procurement, construction and management contract for the $237-million Cerro Vanguardia gold mine in Argentina, a project source said Thursday.
Fluor Daniel SADE is a joint-venture between U.S. firm Fluor Corp and Argentina's SADE.
Cerro Vanguardia is being developed by Minera Mincorp SA, owned 50-percent each by Luxembourg-based Minorco SA and local conglomerate Perez Companc, in the Patagonian province of Santa Cruz.
Fluor Daniel SADE will soon begin work on detailed engineering but there is still no firm timetable for the mine's construction, the source, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The mine would produce around 220,000 ounces a year of gold and 50 tonnes of silver, Roberto Traba, president of site owners Fomecruz, said in September.
